question: What are Stellar Limits Proposals (SLPs), how do they differ from CAPs and SEPs, and how does an approved one take effect?

golden.answer: A Stellar Limits Proposal (SLP) proposes changes to network-configuration limits and fees, such as Soroban ledger caps; it is neither a CAP nor a SEP and lives under limits/ in stellar-protocol. An approved SLP takes effect through a validator-voted configuration upgrade, not a protocol-version change. SLP-0007, for example, raised dependent clusters from 2 to 3 and halved Soroban resource fees, live on Mainnet from 2026-10-22.
keyFacts: SLPs propose network-configuration limit and fee changes; they are not CAPs or SEPs.
An approved SLP takes effect through a validator-voted configuration upgrade.
Document status and network application are separate states.
avoid: Do NOT call an SLP a CAP or SEP.
golden.notes: Accept any current SLP example if dated.
